_why: ITEM 5 WANTS A PICTURE PER COMPONENT, 'rendered on a real frame at reference scale'. These twenty-seven are the ones Builder 2 ported. Every one is a frame of the SAME timeline at the SAME canvas on the SAME corpus fixture, so they are comparable to each other rather than each being its own demo — that is what reference scale buys. The frame was chosen per component from its OWN curves, at the moment its mechanism is legible, and is recorded here with the reason; a frame picked from the middle by habit showed Stack's furniture instead of its plate and is the reason that field exists.

DipToBlack.why_this_frame: the seam itself — full black is the mechanism
DipToBlack.looked_at: FRAME OUTSIDE THE COMPONENT'S WINDOW — a verdict about the SAMPLE, not the component. Every transition and overlay runs 10-30 frames at the START of its item (DipToBlack 10, ShutterFlashOverlay 12, ZoomThrough 14, CardSwipe/SlideOver 16, LightLeakOverlay 20) and the build sampled a FIXED 60-frame stride, so every sample lands past the end of the ramp. What the frame shows is the settled B-side, and what the difference-from-control MEASURES is the A-to-B clip swap — not whether the effect rendered. THE SHARPEST CASE: f300 was shot as the midpoint and should be PURE BLACK. It is a fully lit frame. Not a failed dip — a frame 290 frames past a 10-frame window, where progress clamps to 1 and only the B-side shows. Its 87.96% is entirely the clip swap.

proof_frame.why_this_family: its CORRECT output at the dip is a black frame, which is byte-for-byte what a completely failed render produces. No single frame at the dip can separate them, and no noise floor can either: the correct output has no signal in it to measure.

corroborating.why: MEASURED, not substituted for the ruling: the ease is cubic-bezier (0.55, 0, 0.85, 0.2), which is back-loaded, so 25% carries only 9.6% of the fade. That clears any noise floor and is the weak end of the ramp. 0.40 is offered as the stronger second frame, not in place of the ruled one.

_state_contract: DRAWS = a human-equivalent LOOK at the frame, described, and nothing wrong with it. DEFECT = it draws and the picture is wrong; named, and NOT on the menu. PASSTHROUGH_SUSPECT = indistinguishable from no effect at the frame sampled — a verdict about the FRAME CHOICE, not yet about the component. UNDECIDABLE = the correct output and a failed render are the same image (DipToBlack at its midpoint is black); one frame cannot decide it. STALE_BODY = the still is real and photographs code that has since been re-authored. FILE_ONLY = a sha and no recorded look. Absence of a row is UNKNOWN, never BLANK. ONLY DRAWS REACHES THE MENU.
_body_binding: Every row carries body_sha256_16: the sha of the port/bodies/*.jsx that DREW THIS FRAME. THE ROW RECORDS WHAT WAS SEEN; lane_contract.live_set() DERIVES WHETHER IT STILL APPLIES, by re-hashing the body on disk at read time. So re-authoring a component invalidates its picture the instant the file changes, with nobody remembering to. WITHOUT IT A STILL SILENTLY CERTIFIES SUPERSEDED CODE: seven of these photograph bodies I re-authored in 43b47b4 hours later, and every one of those frames still looks perfectly good. TWO MISTAKES WHILE BUILDING THIS, BOTH KEPT AS THE RECORD. First I backfilled the CURRENT sha onto every row, which made three stills taken before the contain switch pass the staleness check and sit on the menu — a hash carries no evidence of its own currency. Then I hand-wrote STALE_BODY into the seven rows, which SHADOWED the sha check and left the mechanism with no population at all: it was dead, and the red proof exposed it by mutating the binding away and watching nothing go red.
_proof_frame_contract: A COMPONENT WHOSE CORRECT OUTPUT AT ITS MIDPOINT CARRIES NO SIGNAL IS PROVEN SOMEWHERE ELSE ON ITS RAMP (Zac, 2026-09-21). DipToBlack at its dip is black, which is exactly what a failed render looks like, so the frame everybody naturally samples is the one frame that can never decide it. `proof_frame` records WHERE on the ramp the signal exists, what the plate should read there, and what it is compared AGAINST — the same frame with the transition absent. Two comparisons are needed and one frame serves both: PRESENT separates it from a failed render, CHANGED separates it from a passthrough. The family is derived from the bodies — a black root plus complementary A/B opacity fades — not hand-listed, so a component that acquires the shape is covered the day it does.
_frame_window_finding: A DIFFERENCE FROM A CONTROL SAYS SOMETHING CHANGED, NEVER THAT THE EFFECT RENDERED. Builder 1's build is sound — two independent exports are bit-identical at a component-free frame, so the floor really is 0.0000% — and the transition numbers are still nearly meaningless, because for a transition the largest change in the frame is WHICH CLIP IS SHOWING. DipToBlack scored 87.96% on a frame that should have been black and was fully lit. A transition's proof frame must be computed from its own window — start = seamRoom - duration/2, then a chosen progress across `duration` — never from a fixed stride.
